Why train here

What this provider site sets out. No pass rate, award or review score is shown.

  • The course, stated plainly

    Who it is for, what it leads to, and how the training runs, before anyone is asked to commit.

  • Courses matched to a base

    Each course lists the example bases that run it. A base does not advertise training it does not offer.

  • Practical and classroom routes

    Licence training is time in the vehicle. Driver CPC, ADR and Operator CPC are set out as their own courses.

  • A straight enquiry

    The form asks for a course, a preferred base and how you would like to be contacted. It does not book a test.

How training works

Four steps. Course length is confirmed when you enquire.

  1. Say what you want to drive

    Category C, Category C+E, Driver CPC, or one of the further courses. If you are not sure, say so.

  2. Check the licence you hold

    The current entitlement decides the medical, theory and practical steps. Nothing on this site confirms that a particular person qualifies.

  3. Train at the base that offers it

    Each course lists the example bases where it runs. A base does not list a course it does not offer.

  4. Prepare for the next step

    That may be a practical test or periodic training hours. How booking works is explained when you enquire. No result is claimed here.

Guides

Plain explanations of the licence, the medical and the test, with links to the relevant course pages.

  • Guide

    Which HGV licence do I need?

    The licence depends on the vehicle you want to drive, and on what you already hold. This guide separates the main goods-vehicle entitlements from Driver CPC. It does not confirm that you qualify.

  • Guide

    Category C vs Category C+E

    Category C and Category C+E are both goods-vehicle entitlements. One is the rigid lorry. The other adds a trailer. They are trained and tested separately.

  • Guide

    How HGV training works

    HGV training is a sequence, not a single lesson. You say what you want to drive, the licence you already hold is checked, and the medical, theory and practical steps are planned around that. No duration is stated here.

All guides

Questions

Which licence do I need?

Category C is the usual route onto a rigid lorry. Category C+E adds a trailer. Driver CPC is the professional qualification, not a vehicle category. The HGV training page compares them.

Do you publish prices?

No fee is listed. Ask for a quote for the course you want. Medicals, theory tests and the practical test are separate where they apply.

Where does the training take place?

At the example bases in Bristol, Taunton and Exeter. Not every course runs at every base. No street address is published.

Are the reviews real?

No. The quotations are examples for the layout. No rating and no review count are shown.

Is this a real training company?

No. This is a demonstration website by Webco Media. The courses, bases, reviews and contact details are examples.

What happens after I enquire?

You choose a course, a preferred example base and a contact method. The form does not book a test, and on this demonstration it does not send a message.

Ask about a course

Say which course you want, which example base you prefer, and how you would like to be contacted.
